title: Restriction of Hom objects of a hypercover along an inclusion of finite simplicial sets is a covering
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $K$ be a hypercover of $X$ in the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]: a simplicial object of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ each of whose terms $K_n$ covers its matching object $M_n(K)$. Let $A\subseteq B$ be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with $A_n$ and $B_n$ finite and nonempty for every $n\geq0$ and with $A$ and $B$ having finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Then the restriction morphism $\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] is a covering in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$. Thus for every object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every $T$-point $a$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ (a compatible family of $T$-points of the $K_n$, one for each simplex of $A$) there are a covering family $\{T_c\to T\}_{c}$ of $X_{\Et}$ and $T_c$-points $b_c$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0$ whose restrictions are the restrictions $a|_{T_c}$ of $a$.

source.place: Lemma 01GN (lemma-add-simplices), statement and proof using Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex); the missing simplex is lifted along the matching cover

proof.text: *Chain of one-simplex extensions.* By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-add-simplices] there is a chain of simplicial subsets $A=W^0\subseteq W^1\subseteq\dots\subseteq W^r=B$ such that each inclusion $W^k\subseteq W^{k+1}$ adds one simplex $x_k\in W^{k+1}_{n_k}$ subject to conditions (1)-(3) there. Each $W^k$ satisfies the hypotheses needed for $\operatorname{Hom}(W^k,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object]: $A_n\subseteq W^k_n\subseteq B_n$, so $W^k_n$ is finite and nonempty; and a simplex $y\in W^k_m$ that is nondegenerate in $W^k$ is nondegenerate in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]: if $y=B(f)(z)$ with $f:[m]\to[p]$, $p<m$, $z\in B_p$, factor $f=\iota\circ f'$ with $f':[m]\to[p']$ surjective and $\iota:[p']\to[p]$ injective, $p'\leq p<m$, so that $y=B(f')(z')$ with $z'=B(\iota)(z)$; let $g:[p']\to[m]$, $g(l)=\min f'^{-1}(l)$, an order-preserving section of $f'$; then $z'=B(f'\circ g)(z')=B(g)(y)\in W^k_{p'}$ because $W^k$ is a simplicial subset, and $y=W^k(f')(z')$ is degenerate in $W^k$. Hence the nondegenerate simplices of $W^k$ are among the finitely many nondegenerate simplices of $B$.

source.place: Lemma 018S (lemma-add-simplices), cited in the proof of hypercovering.tex Lemma 01GN

proof.text: *Each extension gives a covering.* For $0\leq k<r$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-one-more-simplex] to the hypercover $K$ and the inclusion $U=W^k\subseteq V=W^{k+1}$ with $n=n_k$, $x=x_k$: by step 1 both have finite nonempty sets of simplices in each degree and finitely many nondegenerate simplices, and conditions (1)-(3) hold by the choice of the chain. Hence the restriction morphism $\rho_k:\operatorname{Hom}(W^{k+1},K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(W^k,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] is a covering in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object].

source.place: Lemma 01GM (lemma-one-more-simplex), cited in the proof of Lemma 01GN

proof.text: *Composition.* The restriction morphism $\rho:\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ equals $\rho_0\circ\rho_1\circ\dots\circ\rho_{r-1}$: both are morphisms $\rho'$ with $u^A_s\circ\rho'=u^B_s$ for every simplex $s$ of $A$ (for the composite, apply the defining equation of each $\rho_k$ in turn, as $s\in A\subseteq W^k$ for all $k$), and such a morphism is unique by the universal property of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object]. If $r=0$ then $A=B$ and $\rho$ is the identity, which is a covering since each one-member family $\{\mathrm{id}:V_j\to V_j\}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. If $r\geq1$, induction on $r$ with [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-covering-permanence](1) shows that the composite of the coverings $\rho_k$ of step 2 is a covering.

source.place: Lemma 01GN (lemma-add-simplices), proof (composition of the coverings of Lemma 01GM; Lemma 01G4 (1))

proof.text: *Local lifting.* Write $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0=\{L_j\}_{j\in J}$, $\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0=\{M_i\}_{i\in I}$ and $\rho=(\alpha,(g_i))$. A $T$-point $a$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ is a pair $(j,t)$ with $t:T\to L_j$ an $X$-morphism [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Since $\rho$ is a covering (step 3), $\{g_i:M_i\to L_j\}_{\alpha(i)=j}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$, i.e. a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $T_i=T\times_{t,L_j,g_i}M_i$ for $\alpha(i)=j$; these fibre products are objects of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] the projections $p_i:T_i\to T$ are etale and jointly surjective, so $\{p_i:T_i\to T\}_{\alpha(i)=j}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$. The $T_i$-point $b_i=(i,q_i)$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0$, $q_i:T_i\to M_i$ the second projection, has image $\rho(b_i)=(j,g_i\circ q_i)=(j,t\circ p_i)$, the restriction $a|_{T_i}$ of $a$. By [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object] these points are the compatible families described in the statement.
